evals.prompt: Design the agent for this: a log-triage assistant that reads a failing service's recent logs, calls a search tool over our runbooks and a tool that opens a ticket, and keeps investigating until it can name a likely cause. It uses Claude.
evals.expected_output: An '## Agentic design' section written to docs/design/agentic-design.md, covering Loop, Tools and steps, State and graph, Eval plan (with a parseable JSON block), Harness and Open questions, followed by a proposed git add/commit block that is not run.
expectations: The loop has explicit bounds (max steps, retries, time or cost) expressed as named config values, not numbers inside a prompt
Each of the two tools (runbook search, open ticket) has a contract row, and the ticket tool is identified as having a side effect with retries made safe or forbidden
The Eval plan contains a fenced json block with gate.pass_rate, gate.min_cases, harness.command, harness.replays_against and a cases array
Every eval case has a non-empty 'discriminates' field naming a plausible wrong behaviour, and at least one case uses must_not_contain
No orchestration framework is chosen as settled; the framework choice appears under Open questions
The skill printed a git add/commit block and did not run git

evals.prompt: Design the agentic parts for this: a REST service that stores customer addresses and validates postcodes against a lookup table.
evals.expected_output: A one-line report that the system is not agent-shaped, naming the signal looked for, and no file written.
expectations: No '## Agentic design' section was written anywhere
The report states the system is not agent-shaped and why (no model deciding what to do next, no tool calling, no loop)
No loop bound, tool contract or eval plan was invented

evals.prompt: Add the agent loop, tools and evals to the spec at specs/001-support-bot/spec.md. The bot answers customer questions from our docs and can escalate to a human. The intent does not say which model or framework to use.
evals.expected_output: The '## Agentic design' section added to specs/001-support-bot/spec.md itself, not to docs/design/, with model and framework under Open questions and harness.command set to TBD if no entrypoint is known.
expectations: The section was written into the named spec file, not docs/design/agentic-design.md
Both the model and the orchestration framework are listed under Open questions rather than chosen
If the agent's entrypoint is unknown, harness.command is "TBD" with a matching Open question, not an invented command
Escalation to a human is treated as a tool or step with a stated failure mode
